acceptance: Each of the seven prompts and the server instructions name only tools present in the local-mode tool registry, and every argument used in an example exists in that tool's input schema.
Durable-job tool names (start_benchmark and its siblings) appear only in text that states they need authenticated remote mode.
A test derives the allowed tool and argument names from the live registry, not from a hard-coded list. The PR shows it failing on the pre-fix text and passing after.
scripts/verify_mcp_conformance.py and the doc-contract check pass, and a changelog.d fragment is present.
Smoke: start benchbox-mcp over stdio, fetch every prompt, and show that each named tool resolves in tools/list.
The server instructions and the run_benchmark description tell the model to call validate_results before reporting a run, and give the comparability rule in one sentence consistent with the README.

Any sentence about scale follows the recorded subscale policy (benchbox/core/results/subscale_policy.py): TPC-H and TPC-DS runs below scale factor 1 are unofficial subscale results and remain ranked. No sentence says a subscale run cannot be ranked.
The size of the instructions plus all tool definitions is reported before and after in characters; growth above 15 percent is justified in the PR.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence: a search of benchbox/mcp for function definitions named validate_config, list_recent_runs, compare_results, list_platforms or list_benchmarks finds none registered as tools; list_available and analyze_results are registered. The published MCP reference lists 12 local tools while an internal scan counted 16; record the true count in the PR but do not reconcile the docs here.

Decision gate (before editing): list the registered tools in local and remote mode and map each stale name to its replacement. If a prompt step has no equivalent capability, delete the step and say so in the PR; never invent a tool to make the prompt true.

Verification rubric: pass only if the new test fails without the text fix, the stdio smoke resolves every name, and no file outside benchbox/mcp, its tests and changelog.d changes.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: priority lowered to medium because people, not headless agents, invoke prompts. An earlier draft rule that a run below scale factor 1 'is not a ranking' contradicted the subscale ranking decision and is removed. Local tools/list returns 12 tools.
description:
Problem: the prompts built in benchbox/mcp/prompts/registry.py instruct the model to call validate_config, list_recent_runs, compare_results, list_platforms and list_benchmarks. None is a registered tool. The registered equivalents are run_benchmark(validate_only=True), get_results, analyze_results and list_available. An agent that follows a prompt gets tool-not-found errors or improvises.

Outcome: every tool name and argument name used in every prompt and in the server instructions (MCPServer instructions in benchbox/mcp/server.py) resolves against the server's own registry, and a test keeps it that way.

Non-goals: no tool is added, renamed or removed; no tool schema changes; no new methodology: added guidance may only restate recorded policy.

Also in scope (merged from mcp-instructions-carry-methodology-20261112): the server instructions and the run_benchmark description tell the model to validate a run before reporting it and state when two results are comparable.
